:::{#def-consistent-system}
#### Consistent linear system

A linear system (@def-linear-system) $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$,
with $\matr{A}$ an $m \times n$ matrix and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$,
is **consistent** if it has at least one solution $\vecf{x} \in \reals^n$,
and **inconsistent** otherwise.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-consistent-system}
#### A consistent system and an inconsistent one

With $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\matr{A}\,(x_1, x_2) = (x_1, 0)$ (@def-matvec-mult).

- $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (2, 0)$ is consistent: $\vecf{x} = (2, 0)$ is a solution.
- $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (2, 1)$ is inconsistent:
  the second entry of $\matr{A} \vecf{x}$ is always $0$, never $1$.

:::
